title: M365 BEC: illicit OAuth consent grant for post-reset persistence

source.telemetry: Microsoft Entra ID audit log (Consent to application)
source.detection: Consent granted to a non-gallery multitenant app requesting mail scopes, from an unfamiliar session
source.provenance_note: Entra-sourced, not endpoint. OAuth consent grants appear in the Entra audit log and Microsoft Graph, never in Sysmon, so no Wazuh rule is claimed for this scenario.

intel.campaign: Illicit consent grant / OAuth persistence following AiTM BEC
intel.summary: After stealing a session, the attacker registers or reuses a multitenant OAuth application and induces consent for mail-read and offline-access scopes. The resulting refresh token is independent of the user's password, so it survives a password reset and, depending on configuration, an MFA re-registration too.
intel.scale_note: Microsoft documented a single financially-motivated actor creating roughly 17,000 multitenant OAuth applications and sending over 927,000 phishing emails through the resulting access.
observed_kill_chain: Attacker directs the compromised session to an OAuth consent URL
Consent granted for Mail.Read, Mail.Send, offline_access
Refresh token issued -- persistence no longer depends on the password
Mailbox read and phishing sent from the legitimate tenant

technique: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Application Access Token

alert.description: M365 BEC: consent granted to unverified multitenant app requesting mail and offline-access scopes

fields.RelatedActivity: Same session that created inbox rule 23 minutes earlier

analyst_note: offline_access is the field that matters most -- it is what mints the refresh token that outlives a password reset. PublisherVerified=False on an app requesting Mail.Send is close to conclusive on its own.
